channel.title: FTAS News & Insights
channel.description: Tax law updates, estate planning insights, and fiduciary guidance from Fiduciary Tax & Accounting Services.

item.title: Trusts Hit the 37% Tax Bracket at Just $16,000 in 2026 — Here's How Trustees Can Avoid Overpaying
item.description: A trust reaches the top 37% federal tax bracket at only $16,000 of income in 2026 — a threshold an individual wouldn't hit until earning over $626,000. With the third-quarter estimated tax deadline approaching on September 15, here's why trust brackets are so compressed and the distribution strategy trustees can use to avoid unnecessary tax.

item.title: The IRS Just Labeled a Popular Charitable Trust Strategy a 'Listed Transaction' — Here's What Trustees Need to Know
item.description: New final regulations identify a specific charitable remainder annuity trust structure as an abusive 'listed transaction,' triggering IRS disclosure duties and steep penalties for trustees and beneficiaries who used it. If your CRAT involved a single premium immediate annuity, a 90-day disclosure clock may already be running.

item.title: Trump Accounts Are Open: What Parents and Grandparents Should Know
item.description: As of July 4, 2026, anyone can contribute to a Trump account for a child under 18. Here's how the new accounts actually work — the contribution limits, the investment restrictions, the $1,000 federal seed money, and the tax treatment most coverage glosses over.

item.title: Contributing to a Trump Account? The Gift Tax Rule to Know Before You Do
item.description: Under the tax code as written, every contribution to a Trump account is technically a gift of a future interest — which would normally require a Form 709 filing no matter how small the gift. New IRS guidance creates a safe harbor, but it comes with conditions that are easy to trip.

item.title: The Estate Tax Exemption Just Got Bigger — And This Time It's Permanent
item.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill permanently raised the federal estate and gift tax exemption to $15 million per person. Here's what that means for estates, surviving spouses, and anyone who was waiting on the old sunset.

item.title: The Portability Deadline Most Families Miss — And What It Costs Them
item.description: Filing Form 706 to preserve the Deceased Spousal Unused Exclusion is one of the most valuable elections in estate tax law — and one of the most frequently missed. Here's what it is, why it matters, and what happens if the deadline passes.

item.title: Inherited IRAs in 2026: The 10-Year Rule and What Beneficiaries Need to Know
item.description: The SECURE Act fundamentally changed how inherited IRAs work for most beneficiaries. Four years in, there's still widespread confusion — including about whether annual distributions are required during the 10-year period.

item.title: QCDs Are More Valuable Than Ever in 2026 — Here's Why
item.description: The One Big Beautiful Bill changed the rules on charitable deductions for itemizers — which makes Qualified Charitable Distributions from IRAs an even more powerful tool for retirees who give to charity.
